newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates stabilise ahead of the weekend.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates stabilise ahead of the weekend.

text.p: Dutch money market rates stabilised at the usual level near the advances rate just ahead of the weekend with the market taking in the appropriate allocation of over four billion guilders under the new special advances pact.
The Dutch central bank said earlier it had allocated 4.27 billion guilders to the money market under a seven-day special advances pact at an unchanged rate of 3.00 percent.
Individual banks received 16.5 percent of the amount they had applied for, with a ceiling of 4.0 billion guilders.
"There is enough liquidity around after this allocation," said one dealer.
The dealer added he did not foresee extreme tightness just ahead of the cash reserve expiry on Friday, July 25.
Call money was bid at 3.00 percent or just above this level on Friday and dealers said overnight money would probably stick to this level.

Earlier this week call money had been bid as high as 3.50 percent with an occasional higher settlement. "This should not have happened," said one dealer, adding some players had been sitting on their liquidity with others being somewhat short.

Dealers did not foresee a shortage of liquidity in the days to come and they said players were expected to have their books in balance ahead of the cash reserve expiry, which runs for four or five weeks.
Last month the Dutch central bank decided to provide extra liquidity only one day ahead of the previous expiry of the cash reserve facility.

It offered a currency swap of almost 600 million guilders to ease the shortage of liquidity in the market. "There is no real search for liquidity going on. It's stable and quiet," said one dealer, giving an impression of the need for liquidity.
One-month deposits were bid at an unchanged 3.18 percent and three-month deposits were stuck at 3.20 percent.
The guilder was slightly stronger versus the German mark, trading at 112.585 per 100 marks from 112.605 at yesterday's fixing.
